elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted language: "may, no more than once per year, upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice". Note the cap is expressed as "per year" rather than "in any 12-month period", which on a calendar-year reading could in theory permit inspections in successive Decembers/Januaries; substantively it operates as an annual frequency cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" — written notice, 30 days, exceeds the fallback 15-day requirement.
Retained: "during the Company's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspecting person is "HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined)" — a Vendor employee, not an independent third-party auditor. No operative language substitutes or permits an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered contains no confidentiality obligation binding the inspecting person; no such obligation was added and none is cited from elsewhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site/remote-copy preference appears in the rendered clause; inspection of "the records of the Company's General Manager" is unqualified as to location.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." Vendor bears cost unconditionally, with no shifting trigger at all, which is at least as favourable as the 5% carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the right granted is limited to inspecting "the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments"; no systems-access or remote-access right is conferred here or, per the finding, elsewhere, so there is nothing to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Operation inserted "no more than once per year" into the grant of the inspection right, curing the previously unlimited frequency.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained language: "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained language: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — Vendor bears cost with no underpayment shift-back, i.e. better than the fallback.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single insertion supplies the missing annual frequency cap, while the retained 30-day written notice and unconditional HDI-borne cost sentence already satisfy (and exceed) the other two fallback elements.

Preferred level is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need operative language that (a) permits inspection by an independent third-party auditor rather than "HDI's General Manager", (b) expressly binds that auditor to confidentiality obligations, and (c) requires the inspection to be conducted off-site where reasonably possible. These are not pursued, which is a defensible scoping choice for a records-only inspection right.

Minimality holds: the redline adds only the words "no more than once per year," and deletes nothing. Favourable existing terms (30 days' written notice, normal-business-hours limit, records-only scope, HDI bearing its own inspection fees) are all preserved, and no extras (procedures, survival, expense allocation, damages) were added.

Intent is preserved: the payment-verification purpose, the General Manager references, the defined terms and the cost sentence survive without contradiction; no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is introduced. Comma placement around the inserted phrase reads cleanly.

Optional polish (not required for fallback completeness): express the cap as "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period" to close the calendar-year gap and align exactly with the preferred wording.

Classification as a deviation is correct: unlimited inspection frequency fails the fallback on a material term and edges toward the walk-away trigger for unlimited audits, notwithstanding that notice and cost allocation were already compliant.
Margin comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice, and correctly identifies the single defect cured.
